content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of phloem tissue
Explain the importance of translocation for plants

is the transport of sugars and other organic compounds through phloem tissue. Unlike transpiration in xylem (which is passive), translocation requires energy. It moves substances from where they're made (sources) to where they're needed (sinks).
= transport of organic solutes through phloem
Depends on where substances are needed
Where sugars are made or released from storage
Where sugars are used or stored
Same organ can be source or sink
Potato tuber is a sink in summer (storing starch)
Potato tuber is a source in spring (releasing sugar for growth)
